instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: A 17-year-old scoring in the Premier League; a serious prospect rather than a finished player.
Seventeen goals in a Birmingham side that created little; sharp movement and two-footed finishing. His best season by a distance.
A serious knee injury in the autumn wrecked the season and he was never the same player — rated below the previous year rather than at it.
Eighteen league goals, second only to Drogba, and the sharpest finisher outside the top four that season.
Thirty-one, out of condition and out of the side by Christmas. The finishing was still there; almost nothing else was.
Returned to Oldham in a swap deal early in 1993/94.
A converted right-back filling in during a fifteen-point season; not yet the centre-half he became.
A World Cup winner at his peak and, for half a decade either side of it, the best attacking left-back in the world.
An ever-present in the meanest defence outside the top four that season; big, aggressive and dominant in the air, and briefly an England contender.
Ten goals and six assists in an ever-present season — much the best of his English career, and the year the link play produced something.
Scored the goal that won the title at Old Trafford in a double season; a France starter at his peak.
A France international and European champion used as a rotation forward at 29; still a quality top-four attacker rather than a squad filler.
On loan in a badly beaten side and still good enough to be called into the England squad; the rating is for the keeper, not the goals conceded.
An ever-present and the man of the match in a League Cup final win; the best run of form of his career.
Bought from Inter at twenty-one on the strength of genuinely frightening acceleration, and eleven league goals in his first season here.
Ten goals from the left and, until Christmas, the best player in the league; the move to City the following summer was priced off this season.
World class: pace, strength and reading combined, and in 1998/99 in the conversation for the best centre-back in Europe. Rated above Adams (88) and just under Ferdinand 2007/08 (91).
An Achilles rupture cost him the first half of the season and he was sold that summer; still world class when he played, a point off his peak.
The engine of a promoted side that finished eighth: thirty-six starts, and the best passer in it.
The best season of his career: an ever-present driving midfielder with nine goals for a mid-table side, and City’s outstanding player.
